response: Yes, pain is a clinically relevant problem in general adult psychiatry. Many patients with psychiatric disorders, such as depression and anxiety, often experience chronic pain, which can exacerbate their psychiatric symptoms and reduce their quality of life. Additionally, some psychiatric medications can have pain as a side effect, and unmanaged pain can lead to increased distress, decreased treatment adherence, and poorer mental health outcomes. Therefore, assessing and managing pain is an essential aspect of comprehensive care in general adult psychiatry.
